<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask commands` from the qs-commands registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

# Commands

Every command in QuakeC Studio's command registry (PRIN-3): the one list behind the menus, keystrokes, command palette, CLI, agent tools and MCP tools. Each command has a stable id and takes one JSON object as its parameters, described by the JSON Schema (2020-12) below. Commands that change state can be undone with `edit.undo`.

| Command | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`checkpoint.create`](#checkpointcreate) | Records every file of the open project, as it is on disk, as a checkpoint to restore, in a git store of its own. |
| [`checkpoint.list`](#checkpointlist) | Lists the open project's checkpoints, oldest first. |
| [`checkpoint.restore`](#checkpointrestore) | Puts every file of the open project back as a checkpoint holds it, removing the files made since and dropping unsaved edits, the open map's among them: the map is read again from its file, or closed when the file was made since. |
| [`code.actions`](#codeactions) | Lists the quick fixes for the diagnostics at a place in a file: a missing builtin declared, a misspelled field corrected, an unused local removed, a missing precache added. |
| [`code.fix`](#codefix) | Applies a quick fix for the diagnostics at a place in a file, the first unless one is named by its index in code.actions' list; the file is not saved. |
| [`commands.list`](#commandslist) | Lists every command with its id, summary and parameter schema. |
| [`edit.accept`](#editaccept) | Accepts staged hunks: their lines stay in the editor's text, unsaved, once each hunk of their file is decided. |
| [`edit.accept_next`](#editaccept_next) | Makes the next suggested edit, giving the next place that says the old name the new one, in the editor's text of its file; nothing is saved. Tab in the code editor runs it. |
| [`edit.dismiss_next`](#editdismiss_next) | Drops the suggested edits. Escape in the code editor runs it. |
| [`edit.next`](#editnext) | Answers the next edit the last one implies: after a field's, a function's or a global's name is typed over where it is first declared, the next place that still says the old name, and how many are left. |
| [`edit.redo`](#editredo) | Makes the most recently undone change again. |
| [`edit.reject`](#editreject) | Rejects staged hunks: the lines they replaced come back, byte for byte. |
| [`edit.repeat`](#editrepeat) | Makes the most recent map edit once more: same command, same arguments. |
| [`edit.stage_change`](#editstage_change) | Stages a change to several files as hunks to accept or reject one by one; the project is checked with them, and nothing is written to disk. |
| [`edit.staged`](#editstaged) | Lists the staged hunks waiting to be accepted or rejected. |
| [`edit.undo`](#editundo) | Takes back the most recent change that has not been undone. |
| [`editor.fold`](#editorfold) | Folds the innermost block or block comment at the caret. |
| [`editor.fold_all`](#editorfold_all) | Folds every block and block comment of the open file, each down to its first and last lines. |
| [`editor.go_to_line`](#editorgo_to_line) | Moves the caret to a line of the open file, from 1; without a line it asks for one. |
| [`editor.go_to_symbol`](#editorgo_to_symbol) | Opens a picker of the open file's symbols, to move the caret to one. |
| [`editor.toggle_soft_wrap`](#editortoggle_soft_wrap) | Turns soft wrap on or off: long lines wrap at the editor's width. |
| [`editor.unfold`](#editorunfold) | Unfolds the innermost folded block or comment at the caret. |
| [`editor.unfold_all`](#editorunfold_all) | Unfolds every folded block and block comment of the open file, showing all of its lines. |
| [`engine.builtins`](#enginebuiltins) | Lists an engine's builtins for a module kind, each with its number or engine name, QuakeC name, signature and extensions; the open project's engine and server QuakeC when none is named. |
| [`engine.console`](#engineconsole) | Runs a command in the running game's console and answers the lines it printed. |
| [`engine.inspect`](#engineinspect) | Reads the running game: the edicts in use, one edict's fields, every named global, or the call stack while stopped in a frame. |
| [`engine.screenshot`](#enginescreenshot) | Writes the frame the running game draws as a PNG, in the project's build/screenshots unless a path is given, and answers where and its size. |
| [`file.close`](#fileclose) | Closes a file's tab, opening the tab beside it when it was         the open file; its unsaved text is kept. |
| [`file.format`](#fileformat) | Formats a QuakeC file: each line indented with tabs to its depth, trailing white space removed. Only white space at the ends of lines changes, so it compiles to the same progs.dat; the file is not saved. |
| [`file.inlay_hints`](#fileinlay_hints) | Lists a file's inlay hints: the name of the parameter each argument of a call is passed as. |
| [`file.open`](#fileopen) | Opens a file in the editor, with the caret at a byte offset or at the start. |
| [`file.read`](#fileread) | Reads a file's current text: the editor's when it has unsaved changes, else what is on disk. |
| [`file.replace_all`](#filereplace_all) | Replaces every match of a search in a file and saves it, as one undoable change; matching case, whole words and regular expressions as project.search. |
| [`file.replace_range`](#filereplace_range) | Replaces a byte range of a file's text, in the editor's text; nothing is saved. An edit in an excerpt of the multibuffer. |
| [`file.save`](#filesave) | Writes a file's current text, as the editor has it, to disk. |
| [`file.update`](#fileupdate) | Takes the whole text of a file as an editor has it, unsaved, and checks the project again. |
| [`files.changed`](#fileschanged) | Takes files another program changed: the open map is read again when it has no unsaved edits, else kept for map.resolve_disk_change; changed QuakeC is read again with the entity definitions derived from it. |
| [`git.blame`](#gitblame) | Says who last changed each line of a file, and in which commit. |
| [`git.branches`](#gitbranches) | Lists the repository's local branches, the checked-out one marked. |
| [`git.commit`](#gitcommit) | Commits what is staged with a message; the new commit's id. |
| [`git.conflicts`](#gitconflicts) | Lists a file's merge conflicts: where each one's markers are. |
| [`git.create_branch`](#gitcreate_branch) | Creates a branch at the current commit and checks it out, as git switch -c does. |
| [`git.diff`](#gitdiff) | Lists the hunks of a file's unstaged or staged changes. |
| [`git.head_text`](#githead_text) | Gives a file's text at HEAD, which the editor marks its changes against; none for a file HEAD does not have. |
| [`git.log`](#gitlog) | Lists the commits that changed a file, the newest first, following renames. |
| [`git.resolve`](#gitresolve) | Resolves one of a file's merge conflicts by keeping our side, theirs or both, and saves the file. |
| [`git.stage`](#gitstage) | Stages a file, or one hunk of its unstaged changes. |
| [`git.status`](#gitstatus) | Lists the project repository's branch and changed files, staged and not, as git status does; none when the project is not in a git repository. |
| [`git.switch`](#gitswitch) | Checks out a branch, as git switch does, and reads the project's files again; refused while files have unsaved edits. |
| [`git.unstage`](#gitunstage) | Unstages a file, or one hunk of its staged changes. |
| [`help.about`](#helpabout) | Opens the About window: the app's name, version, copyright and license, and links to its site and its source. |
| [`help.report_issue`](#helpreport_issue) | Opens the page where an issue with the app is reported, in the browser. |
| [`help.user_guide`](#helpuser_guide) | Opens the user guide on the website, in the browser. |
| [`map.accept_hunks`](#mapaccept_hunks) | Accepts hunks of the open map's review, every one when none are named: their change is kept and no longer waits. |
| [`map.add_layer`](#mapadd_layer) | Adds an empty layer to the open map, as TrenchBroom writes one. |
| [`map.add_wad`](#mapadd_wad) | Adds a WAD file to the open map's list in its world's `wad` or `_wad` key, by its path from the map's folder when it is under it, as TrenchBroom adds a WAD dropped on its window; one listed already is not listed again. |
| [`map.apply_fix`](#mapapply_fix) | Applies a quick fix `map.issues` gave, as one step with undo. |
| [`map.backup`](#mapbackup) | Writes the open map, as it is in the editor, saved or not, as its next backup in the autosave folder beside it, keeping the last 20. |
| [`map.backups`](#mapbackups) | Lists the open map's backups in the autosave folder beside it, the newest first. |
| [`map.brush_chamfer`](#mapbrush_chamfer) | Chamfers an edge of a brush into one or more bevel faces, from a distance along each of its two faces (MAP-15.9). |
| [`map.brush_clip`](#mapbrush_clip) | Clips a brush of the open map by the plane through three points, keeping the part behind it, in front of it, or both as two brushes. |
| [`map.brush_create`](#mapbrush_create) | Adds a box brush from two corners, snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| [`map.brush_delete`](#mapbrush_delete) | Deletes a brush of an entity of the open map. |
| [`map.brush_extrude`](#mapbrush_extrude) | Moves a face of a brush along its normal by a distance snapped to the grid, out or in, its texture fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.3). |
| [`map.brush_hollow`](#mapbrush_hollow) | Hollows a brush into walls of a thickness: the brush becomes itself with the brush its walls enclose taken out (MAP-15.5). |
| [`map.brush_hull`](#mapbrush_hull) | Adds to the world, or the entity given, the convex brush around points snapped to the grid, with a texture, as TrenchBroom's complex shape tool makes one. |
| [`map.brush_intersect`](#mapbrush_intersect) | Replaces two or more brushes of an entity with the solid all of them hold, which takes the first's place (MAP-15.6). |
| [`map.brush_merge`](#mapbrush_merge) | Merges two or more brushes of an entity of the open map into their convex hull, which takes the first's place. |
| [`map.brush_move`](#mapbrush_move) | Moves brushes of an entity by an offset snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free. |
| [`map.brush_scale`](#mapbrush_scale) | Scales brushes of an entity by factors along x, y and z about a point, the middle of their bounds unless given, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| [`map.brush_shape`](#mapbrush_shape) | Adds a shape of brushes filling a box, its corners snapped to the grid: a cylinder (solid or hollow), cone, arch, UV or icosahedron spheroid, rock, scalable curve of 12, 24, 48 or 96 sides, or straight or spiral stairs whose default step a player climbs; to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| [`map.brush_shear`](#mapbrush_shear) | Shears brushes of an entity: each point moves along one axis by a factor times its distance from a point along another, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| [`map.brush_split_edge`](#mapbrush_split_edge) | Splits an edge of a brush by a new vertex at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the edge's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| [`map.brush_split_face`](#mapbrush_split_face) | Splits a face of a brush by a new vertex in front of it, at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the face's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| [`map.brush_subtract`](#mapbrush_subtract) | Subtracts a brush of the open map from every other brush of its entity, then deletes it: the brushes it overlapped become the parts outside it. |
| [`map.brush_sweep`](#mapbrush_sweep) | Sweeps a brush along a path of points snapped to the grid: the brush becomes one brush for each step, the hull of it at the step's two ends (MAP-15.4). |
| [`map.brush_texture`](#mapbrush_texture) | Sets the texture, shift, rotation or scale of every face of brushes of an entity, keeping what is not given (MAP-12). |
| [`map.brush_vertex`](#mapbrush_vertex) | Moves a vertex of a brush of the open map to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the convex hull of its vertices so moved. |
| [`map.brush_vertices`](#mapbrush_vertices) | Moves several vertices of a brush at once, each to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the hull of its vertices so moved (MAP-15.7). |
| [`map.brushes`](#mapbrushes) | Lists the brushes of an entity of the open map, the world's when none is named: each brush's place, which the map.brush_* tools take, the box around it and its textures; all of them, or those touching a box. The brush tools answer the places of the brushes they make, so this is for brushes whose places are not known: a map someone else built, or after a tool that changed how many brushes the entity has. |
| [`map.build_passage`](#mapbuild_passage) | Builds a passage between two doorways of the open map that face each other along x or along y, 112 wide and 128 high, with stairs where their floors differ, a light, and a door when one is asked for. |
| [`map.build_room`](#mapbuild_room) | Builds one room of a shape of id's levels into the open map, sealed but for the doorways asked for, with its lights: a pillared hall, an eight-sided domed chamber, a hall around a pit crossed by bridges, a room on two levels, a courtyard, a cross of two aisles, or a vaulted room. Answers its doorways, for map.build_passage, and where things may stand. |
| [`map.check`](#mapcheck) | Checks a .map: what id's qbsp and ericw-tools read otherwise, and its entities against the project's server QuakeC as the engine reads them: unknown classnames and keys with the closest name, values their field cannot read, and targets and targetnames nothing matches. It reads the file alone, so it says a world that names no WAD is one as id's qbsp does; map.issues and map.find_leaks say whether a texture of the open map is missing. |
| [`map.choose_profile`](#mapchoose_profile) | Chooses the compile profile map.run_profile runs when given none; none given chooses Full again. |
| [`map.compare_with_disk`](#mapcompare_with_disk) | How the open map's file, changed by another program, differs from the map being edited, entity by entity. |
| [`map.compile`](#mapcompile) | Compiles the open map, as it is in the editor, or only a region of it, sealed, to a BSP beside it, with its portal and leak files, and reports whether it leaks and the textures its WADs lack. |
| [`map.copy`](#mapcopy) | Writes brushes of the world and whole entities of the open map as a .map's text, where they are, for the clipboard; the map is unchanged. |
| [`map.delete_entity`](#mapdelete_entity) | Deletes an entity of the open map; the world stays. |
| [`map.duplicate_entity`](#mapduplicate_entity) | Duplicates an entity of the open map, its keys and brushes, in place at the end of the map, and selects the copy; the world is not duplicated. A targetname ending in a number takes the next free number, and the keys the code fires entities by move on by as many. |
| [`map.entities_removed_by_skill`](#mapentities_removed_by_skill) | The entities of the open map the game removes at a skill and in a kind of game (single, coop or deathmatch), found by spawning the map with the project's program: those the spawnflags rule out and those the QuakeC removes. |
| [`map.export`](#mapexport) | Writes the open map to another .map without the layers marked to be left out of exports and the entities in them (TrenchBroom's Export). |
| [`map.extract_linked`](#mapextract_linked) | Moves entities of a linked group, and the same entities of every group linked to it, into new groups linked to each other (TrenchBroom's Extract Linked Groups). |
| [`map.face_align`](#mapface_align) | Carries one face's texture alignment onto other faces of the open map, so the texture continues across the line their planes share (MAP-13.8). |
| [`map.face_uv`](#mapface_uv) | Fits, justifies, flips, resets, snaps or adjusts the texture of faces of the open map, at the size its WAD gives it (MAP-13). |
| [`map.find_leaks`](#mapfind_leaks) | Compiles the open map in memory and reports whether it leaks, with the trail from the entity the outside reaches out to the void, and the textures its WADs lack. |
| [`map.flip`](#mapflip) | Mirrors entities and brushes along an axis through the middle of their box: brushes and point entities' origins, and their facing, as TrenchBroom's Flip. |
| [`map.generate`](#mapgenerate) | Makes a random playable level and opens it: rooms of several shapes joined by passages, stairs and doors, from a start to an exit, with lights, monsters, weapons and a key, textured from the game's own levels. One seed gives one level. |
| [`map.group`](#mapgroup) | Puts entities and brushes of the world in a new group, in the layer or group the first is in, as TrenchBroom writes a group. |
| [`map.hide`](#maphide) | Hides entities of the open map in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Hide Selection); the map is not changed. |
| [`map.isolate`](#mapisolate) | Hides every entity of the open map but these in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Isolate Selection); the map is not changed. |
| [`map.issues`](#mapissues) | Lists every issue of the open map, each with the entity or brush it is about and a quick fix where one exists: its format's, brushes with no volume, a missing player start, missing textures and, with a project open, its entities' against the server QuakeC. |
| [`map.layers`](#maplayers) | The open map's TrenchBroom layers: each one's name, whether it is hidden, locked or left out of exports, and how many entities are in it. |
| [`map.link_duplicate`](#maplink_duplicate) | Copies a group and its entities as a new group linked to it, so an edit in one is made in the other (TrenchBroom's Create Linked Duplicate). |
| [`map.link_target`](#maplink_target) | Points a key of an entity of the open map, one the code fires entities by such as target or killtarget, at another entity: the key takes the other's targetname, and the other its classname and the next free number as one when it has none. |
| [`map.list_entities`](#maplist_entities) | The open map's rooms (TrenchBroom's named layers and groups, with their bounds) and its entities: each one's place, classname, origin, targetname and room, filtered by room or classname. |
| [`map.list_textures`](#maplist_textures) | Lists the open map's textures: those of the WADs its world names, found in the project, beside the map or in the game, of the BSP it was opened from, and of the game's own levels, each once with where it comes from, its size and how many faces use it, and the names its faces use that nothing holds. |
| [`map.lock`](#maplock) | Locks entities of the open map against edits until map.unlock_all; the map is not changed. |
| [`map.make_brush_entity`](#mapmake_brush_entity) | Makes brushes of the world a new brush entity of a class, such as func_door (TrenchBroom's Create Brush Entity). |
| [`map.make_structural`](#mapmake_structural) | Gives a brush entity's brushes back to the world, in the layer or group the entity was in, and removes the entity (TrenchBroom's Make Structural). |
| [`map.move_entity`](#mapmove_entity) | Moves an entity of the open map: a point entity's origin, a brush entity's brushes. |
| [`map.move_to_layer_or_group`](#mapmove_to_layer_or_group) | Moves an entity or a group of the open map into a layer or a group, or into the default layer given the world, as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| [`map.new`](#mapnew) | Makes a new .map holding a world with the keys given, and opens it in the map view; a file that is there already is refused. |
| [`map.open`](#mapopen) | Opens a .map in the map view, or a shipped .bsp's entities when the map has no .map source; nothing is selected. |
| [`map.outline`](#mapoutline) | The open map's outline: the default layer and each layer, their groups and linked groups, then their entities by classname and targetname, with brush counts; with filter, only what holds the text and what is around it. |
| [`map.paste`](#mappaste) | Adds a .map's text to the open map, its world's brushes to the world and its other entities after the map's: where the text has them, or with the middle of their floor at a point on the grid. |
| [`map.place_entity`](#mapplace_entity) | Places a point entity of a classname at an origin in the open map, with the keys given, and selects it. |
| [`map.place_prefab`](#mapplace_prefab) | Copies a prefab into the open map with its origin at a point on the grid: its world's brushes into the world, its other entities after the map's. |
| [`map.play_from_here`](#mapplay_from_here) | Compiles the open map fast, with no vis and fast light, into the project's build, starts the game on it and puts the player's eye at a point, facing a way: the map view's camera (MAP-13), or with no eye the map's own player start. It answers where the player was put, the light there and the entities that stand in the dark; with start paused the game waits there with its monsters not yet awake, for a screenshot of the map as it was built. |
| [`map.portals`](#mapportals) | Reads the portal file the open map's last compile wrote beside it, each portal's points, to show where the map's leaves meet. |
| [`map.prefabs`](#mapprefabs) | Lists the .map files in the project's prefabs folder. |
| [`map.profiles`](#mapprofiles) | Lists the compile profiles: the built-in Full and Fast, then the project's own from compile-profiles.toml, each its name and its tasks. |
| [`map.read_entity`](#mapread_entity) | An entity of the open map: its pairs, the keys its class reads with their types and defaults, and the map's targetnames for its target keys. |
| [`map.reject_hunks`](#mapreject_hunks) | Rejects hunks of the open map's review, every one when none are named: the parts they replaced are put back, as an edit undo takes back. |
| [`map.remove_key`](#mapremove_key) | Removes every pair with a key from an entity of the open map. |
| [`map.rename_key`](#maprename_key) | Renames a key in every open .map, keeping each value and its formatting: what to run once the person confirms, after symbol.rename renames a field a map may name. Nothing is saved. |
| [`map.replace_texture`](#mapreplace_texture) | Puts one texture in another's place on the faces of brushes, or of every brush of the map, keeping their alignment (TrenchBroom's Replace Material). |
| [`map.resolve_disk_change`](#mapresolve_disk_change) | After another program changed the open map's file while it had unsaved edits: keep disk to read the file again, or mine to keep the edits and save them over it. |
| [`map.restore_backup`](#maprestore_backup) | Puts a backup of the open map in the editor in place of the map, unsaved, as an edit that undo takes back. |
| [`map.rotate_entity`](#maprotate_entity) | Turns a point entity of the open map about the vertical: its angle, or its angles' yaw. |
| [`map.rotate_objects`](#maprotate_objects) | Turns entities and brushes by degrees about the vertical through the middle of their box, counter-clockwise seen from above: brushes and point entities' origins and facing, as TrenchBroom's Rotate. |
| [`map.run_profile`](#maprun_profile) | Runs a compile profile on the open map, the one chosen when none is named: its tasks in order, each timed, stopping at the first that fails; reports each task's time and result. |
| [`map.save`](#mapsave) | Saves the open map: a .map over itself; a BSP's entities as a .ent beside it (bsp: ent, the default) or into the BSP's entity lump (bsp: lump). |
| [`map.save_prefab`](#mapsave_prefab) | Writes brushes of the world and whole entities of the open map as a prefab in the project's prefabs folder, around the middle of their floor. |
| [`map.search`](#mapsearch) | Finds the open map's objects as TrenchBroom's search does: text found in names, classnames, keys, values, textures, smart tags and layer and group names, ignoring case, or a query in its query language, which finds entities, groups, brushes, the contents of layers, or faces. |
| [`map.select`](#mapselect) | Selects an entity of the open map, or clears the selection. |
| [`map.set_flag`](#mapset_flag) | Sets or clears one spawnflag of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also, in one step, keeping each entity's other flags. |
| [`map.set_key`](#mapset_key) | Sets a key of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also with it in one step: its last occurrence keeps its place and formatting, a new key goes after the others. |
| [`map.set_layer`](#mapset_layer) | Turns a layer of the open map hidden, locked or left out of exports on or off, written as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| [`map.show_all`](#mapshow_all) | Shows every entity of the open map hidden in the editor (TrenchBroom's Show All); a hidden layer stays hidden. |
| [`map.stage`](#mapstage) | Begins review of the open map's edits: the map as it is now is kept, and each edit after it waits as a hunk to accept or reject. The agent's map edits begin it themselves; while it is open it is left as it is. |
| [`map.staged_hunks`](#mapstaged_hunks) | Lists the open map's hunks waiting for review: for each, the entities it is in, and the keys and brushes it adds, changes or removes. |
| [`map.summary`](#mapsummary) | A map in short, to review it or compare it with others: the box around its brushes, its brush and entity counts, its entities counted by classname (monsters, lights, items, triggers), its textures counted by face, and its world's keys. The open map, or with a path a .map file read from the disk without opening it; with `most_textures`, only that many textures of the count it gives, which keeps it short when many maps are read. map.list_entities lists each entity; this counts them. |
| [`map.ungroup`](#mapungroup) | Takes a group's entities and brushes out of it into the layer or group it is in, or the world's, and removes the group. |
| [`map.unlink_group`](#mapunlink_group) | Unlinks a group from the groups linked to it, which then change on their own (TrenchBroom's Separate Linked Groups). |
| [`map.unlock_all`](#mapunlock_all) | Unlocks every entity of the open map locked in the editor; a locked layer stays locked. |
| [`map.unstage`](#mapunstage) | Ends the open map's review when nothing waits in it, as after an agent's map command that changed nothing; a review with hunks is left open. |
| [`model.add_frames`](#modeladd_frames) | Adds frames of another model of the same vertices to the end of a model's own, each by its name: QuakeC's $frame list gains the same names at its end. |
| [`model.copy_from_game`](#modelcopy_from_game) | Copies a model of the game, by its name there such as progs/soldier.mdl, into the project as a file of its own to change: a mod's file of the same name takes the game's place, and one of a new name is a new model. |
| [`model.export_skin`](#modelexport_skin) | Writes a skin of a model as a PNG, in the game's palette, to look at or to paint on and give back with model.set_skin. |
| [`model.import`](#modelimport) | Makes a .mdl model in the project of a mesh in an .obj file (one pose), or an .iqe, .fbx, .md5mesh or .smd file (a frame for each frame of each animation, posed by its skeleton). A mesh with texture coordinates keeps them, on a PNG given as its skin or one colour; one without is laid out front and back, to export, paint and set. |
| [`model.inspect`](#modelinspect) | Reads a .mdl model: its skins, their size and the rows of the palette each is of, its vertices and triangles, the box it fills, and its frames by name in the order QuakeC numbers them, as a $frame line lists them. |
| [`model.move`](#modelmove) | Moves a model against its origin, the point the entity's origin is at: its vertices keep their packed places and the header's origin moves. |
| [`model.recolor`](#modelrecolor) | Recolours a skin of a model by rows of the palette: every pixel of a row becomes the same shade of another row, as the game recolours a player's shirt and trousers. |
| [`model.remove_frames`](#modelremove_frames) | Takes frames out of a model, each by its name. The frames after one taken out are numbered one less, so QuakeC's $frame list loses the same names. |
| [`model.rename_frames`](#modelrename_frames) | Renames frames of a model, each by its name. The game finds a frame by its number, so QuakeC's $frame names are its own: keep them in step. |
| [`model.scale`](#modelscale) | Makes a model larger or smaller about its origin, on each axis: its vertices keep their packed places and the header's step and origin are scaled, so nothing is rounded again. The box QuakeC gives the entity (setsize) is its own to change. |
| [`model.set_skin`](#modelset_skin) | Replaces a skin of a model with a PNG of the skin's size, each changed pixel matched to the nearest of the palette's colours that do not glow in the dark, or to a fullbright colour when it is exactly that colour. |
| [`paths.open`](#pathsopen) | Opens folders as projects, and files in the nearest project above each (a folder holding quakec.toml or progs.src): a .map or .bsp in the map editor, any other file in the editor. A file outside every project opens in the open project, or opens its folder when none is open. |
| [`paths.take_opened`](#pathstake_opened) | Takes what the last paths.open opened, once, or null: the desktop app shows it and comes to the front when another launch sent the paths. |
| [`preview.breakpoint`](#previewbreakpoint) | Adds a breakpoint at a line of a file, or takes it away when there is one; set in the running game too and in each game that starts. |
| [`preview.choose_game`](#previewchoose_game) | Chooses the folder the preview reads the game from, in place, and says what it holds; a folder that cannot be played is not kept. |
| [`preview.console`](#previewconsole) | Runs a command in the running game's console. |
| [`preview.dock`](#previewdock) | Docks the game's window beside the IDE's window, given where the IDE's window is and whether it has the focus. |
| [`preview.game_files`](#previewgame_files) | Says what game data the preview plays from: the chosen folder, or the first install found, as found, shareware only, rerelease only or missing for the game the project is for, with the files it lacks. |
| [`preview.pause`](#previewpause) | Pauses the running game between frames. |
| [`preview.pick`](#previewpick) | Selects the edict under a point of the game's window. A point with no edict under it answers none and leaves the selection as it was. |
| [`preview.play`](#previewplay) | Builds the open project and starts the preview host on its program, stopping a game already running. |
| [`preview.poll`](#previewpoll) | Reads the running game's events: its state changes and console lines. |
| [`preview.reload`](#previewreload) | Builds the open project and reloads its program in the running game, the map going on; nothing when no game runs. |
| [`preview.restart`](#previewrestart) | Starts the running game's map again. |
| [`preview.resume`](#previewresume) | Resumes the paused game. |
| [`preview.select`](#previewselect) | Selects an edict of the running game and reads its fields for the Properties panel. |
| [`preview.set_field`](#previewset_field) | Sets a field of the selected edict while the game is paused, the value read as the field's type. |
| [`preview.step`](#previewstep) | Runs one server frame of the game, pausing it first, and leaves it paused. |
| [`preview.step_by`](#previewstep_by) | Steps the game stopped in a frame by a statement, into a call, over one or out to the caller. |
| [`preview.stop`](#previewstop) | Stops the game. |
| [`preview.unwatch`](#previewunwatch) | Takes a watch away. |
| [`preview.watch`](#previewwatch) | Adds a watch, an expression read each time the game stops in a frame. |
| [`project.build`](#projectbuild) | Compiles each module of the open project, with the editor's text of each open file, and writes its progs.dat and .lno. |
| [`project.check`](#projectcheck) | Lists every error and warning in the open project, as the Problems panel does. |
| [`project.compile`](#projectcompile) | Compiles the open project and says whether it is clean, with its error counts. |
| [`project.entities`](#projectentities) | Lists the entity classes the open project's server QuakeC defines, read from its spawn functions: each class's keys, defaults, spawnflags, comment, model and size; with fgd, also writes them as an FGD file for other map editors. |
| [`project.export`](#projectexport) | Builds the open project and exports it as a zip players install: its programs, its own assets (optionally in pak0.pak), a README and its license notices, never id's game data. |
| [`project.files`](#projectfiles) | Lists every source file the open project compiles, by path. |
| [`project.info`](#projectinfo) | Describes the open project: its directory and each module's kind, dialect, target engine and output. |
| [`project.new`](#projectnew) | Makes a new project from a starter template, id's QuakeC 1.01 or the rerelease's, with quakec.toml, a sample test and the GPLv2 notices; it builds and plays at once. |
| [`project.open`](#projectopen) | Opens the QuakeC project in a directory: its quakec.toml, or its progs.src and csprogs.src. |
| [`project.reference`](#projectreference) | The reference to read before writing or debugging QuakeC or building a map, by topic: quakec (the language, how a mod runs, pitfalls), entities (what the engine calls, movetype and solid, the builtins by purpose, what QuakeC does that C does not, debugging), monsters (how a monster is written and every place a new one is added), models (what a model is, and how to recolour, scale and reframe one), maps, workflow (tests and scenarios). Written from id's QuakeC and the engine's specs; a mod's own code comes first where it differs. |
| [`project.search`](#projectsearch) | Finds every match of a text in the open project's files, unsaved edits included, by file, line and byte range; matching case, whole words only or as a regular expression. |
| [`project.symbols`](#projectsymbols) | Lists the open project's global definitions, functions, globals and fields, each with where its name is first written; a query keeps those whose name contains it. |
| [`project.take_checked`](#projecttake_checked) | Takes the problems, symbols and highlighting the background check worked out for the latest edit, if it has finished; says whether anything changed. |
| [`project.test`](#projecttest) | Builds the open project and runs its tests: each test_ function called alone in the VM over a mock engine, and each scenario under tests/ played in the server simulation, answering each test's verdict. |
| [`scenario.run`](#scenariorun) | Builds the open project and plays a scenario file on it in the server simulation, answering whether each assertion held, with the values read, and writing its screenshots beside it. |
| [`settings.get`](#settingsget) | Gives one setting's value and where it comes from. |
| [`settings.list`](#settingslist) | Lists every setting with its default, its value and where the value comes from. |
| [`settings.open`](#settingsopen) | Opens the user's settings file in the editor, made with nothing set when there is none. |
| [`settings.reset`](#settingsreset) | Removes a setting from the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| [`settings.set`](#settingsset) | Sets a setting in the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| [`symbol.complete`](#symbolcomplete) | Lists the names that may be written at a place. |
| [`symbol.definition`](#symboldefinition) | Finds where the name at a place is defined. |
| [`symbol.hover`](#symbolhover) | Says what the name at a place is: its declaration and its comment. |
| [`symbol.references`](#symbolreferences) | Finds every declaration and use of the name at a place, in every file. |
| [`symbol.rename`](#symbolrename) | Renames the name at a place everywhere it is written, in the editor's text of each file; nothing is saved. |
| [`task.list`](#tasklist) | Lists the open project's tasks: the named command lines of its quakec.toml. |
| [`task.run`](#taskrun) | Runs one of the open project's tasks in a new terminal tab, by the user's shell in the project directory. |
| [`terminal.close`](#terminalclose) | Closes a terminal tab, ending its process. |
| [`terminal.new`](#terminalnew) | Opens the user's shell in the project directory in a new terminal tab. |
| [`terminal.poll`](#terminalpoll) | Takes what the terminal tabs have written and how their processes ended, without waiting; true when any tab changed. |
| [`terminal.send`](#terminalsend) | Writes a line to a terminal tab's shell. |
| [`texture.import`](#textureimport) | Imports a PNG image as a texture: quantized to the game's palette with its mip levels, written into the project's own WAD in textures/, in place of a texture of the same name, and that WAD named in the open map's world. |
| [`view.close_split`](#viewclose_split) | Closes the editor's second pane. |
| [`view.focus_bottom_panel`](#viewfocus_bottom_panel) | Shows the bottom panel, Problems, Console and the debugger, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.focus_command_line`](#viewfocus_command_line) | Gives the command line the keyboard: a command is typed by its id or a short name, and each of its parameters is asked for in turn. |
| [`view.focus_editor`](#viewfocus_editor) | Gives the keyboard to the editor in the centre. |
| [`view.focus_left_panel`](#viewfocus_left_panel) | Shows the left panel, Project and Entities, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.focus_right_panel`](#viewfocus_right_panel) | Shows the right panel, Properties and the agent, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.map_back`](#viewmap_back) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look south at the whole map, from the north. |
| [`view.map_bottom`](#viewmap_bottom) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look up at the whole map from below, north up. |
| [`view.map_camera`](#viewmap_camera) | Sets the map editor's camera: the 3D view's field of view, 50 to 150 degrees, how fast the mouse and keys move it, 0.1 to 10 times, and which way a vertical look and the wheel go. Settings not given are kept. |
| [`view.map_front`](#viewmap_front) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look north at the whole map, from the south. |
| [`view.map_grid`](#viewmap_grid) | Sets the map editor's grid in units, a power of two from 0.125 to 256. |
| [`view.map_grid_step`](#viewmap_grid_step) | Halves or doubles the map editor's grid, held to 0.125 to 256 units. |
| [`view.map_isometric`](#viewmap_isometric) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look at the whole map from the south-west and above. |
| [`view.map_keep_view`](#viewmap_keep_view) | Keeps a place and heading of the map editor's 3D view as a saved view. The window runs it for `view.map_save_view_1` to `_4`, with its camera. |
| [`view.map_left`](#viewmap_left) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look east at the whole map, from the west. |
| [`view.map_orbit_down`](#viewmap_orbit_down) | Turns the map editor's 3D view 15 degrees down about the selection, or about the point ahead when nothing is selected. |
| [`view.map_orbit_left`](#viewmap_orbit_left) | Turns the map editor's 3D view 15 degrees to the left about the selection, or about the point ahead when nothing is selected. |
| [`view.map_orbit_right`](#viewmap_orbit_right) | Turns the map editor's 3D view 15 degrees to the right about the selection, or about the point ahead when nothing is selected. |
| [`view.map_orbit_up`](#viewmap_orbit_up) | Turns the map editor's 3D view 15 degrees up about the selection, or about the point ahead when nothing is selected. |
| [`view.map_pan_down`](#viewmap_pan_down) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 32 units down, keeping its heading. |
| [`view.map_pan_left`](#viewmap_pan_left) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 32 units to its left, keeping its heading. |
| [`view.map_pan_right`](#viewmap_pan_right) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 32 units to its right, keeping its heading. |
| [`view.map_pan_up`](#viewmap_pan_up) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 32 units up, keeping its heading. |
| [`view.map_panes`](#viewmap_panes) | Splits the map view: the 3D view alone, with a top view in its corner, or beside top, front and side views. |
| [`view.map_right`](#viewmap_right) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look west at the whole map, from the east. |
| [`view.map_save_view_1`](#viewmap_save_view_1) | Saves where the map editor's 3D view is as view 1, kept in the layout file. |
| [`view.map_save_view_2`](#viewmap_save_view_2) | Saves where the map editor's 3D view is as view 2, kept in the layout file. |
| [`view.map_save_view_3`](#viewmap_save_view_3) | Saves where the map editor's 3D view is as view 3, kept in the layout file. |
| [`view.map_save_view_4`](#viewmap_save_view_4) | Saves where the map editor's 3D view is as view 4, kept in the layout file. |
| [`view.map_shading`](#viewmap_shading) | Draws the map view's 3D pane as the brushes' edges, as their textured faces, or lit by the last compile's lightmaps. |
| [`view.map_top`](#viewmap_top) | Turns the map editor's 3D view to look down on the whole map from above, north up. |
| [`view.map_view_1`](#viewmap_view_1) | Brings the map editor's 3D view back to saved view 1. |
| [`view.map_view_2`](#viewmap_view_2) | Brings the map editor's 3D view back to saved view 2. |
| [`view.map_view_3`](#viewmap_view_3) | Brings the map editor's 3D view back to saved view 3. |
| [`view.map_view_4`](#viewmap_view_4) | Brings the map editor's 3D view back to saved view 4. |
| [`view.map_zoom_in`](#viewmap_zoom_in) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 64 units forwards along its view. |
| [`view.map_zoom_out`](#viewmap_zoom_out) | Moves the map editor's 3D view 64 units back along its view. |
| [`view.move_panel`](#viewmove_panel) | Moves a panel to another dock, where it shows, as Zed's status-bar menu moves one. |
| [`view.project_search`](#viewproject_search) | Opens the project search: every match in the project's files as a multibuffer of editable excerpts, to edit or replace in place. |
| [`view.resize_panel`](#viewresize_panel) | Sets the width of the left or right panel, or the height of the bottom panel, in points. |
| [`view.show_panel`](#viewshow_panel) | Shows a panel in its dock, opening the dock; when the dock already shows it, hides the dock, as a click on Zed's status-bar button does, unless when_shown is keep. |
| [`view.split_down`](#viewsplit_down) | Splits the editor into two panes, one above the other, the second showing the open file. |
| [`view.split_right`](#viewsplit_right) | Splits the editor into two panes side by side, the second showing the open file. |
| [`view.tab_switcher`](#viewtab_switcher) | Opens the tab switcher: the open files, the one used most recently first. |
| [`view.toggle_embedded_game`](#viewtoggle_embedded_game) | Shows the running game in the window's Game tab, run in the editor's own process, or in the preview host's window beside it; a game that runs is stopped, and the next Play starts it in the place chosen. |
| [`view.toggle_outline`](#viewtoggle_outline) | Shows or hides the outline panel beside the editor: the open file's symbols, the one the caret is in marked. |
| [`view.toggle_panel`](#viewtoggle_panel) | Shows or hides a panel: Project and Entities on the left, Properties and the agent on the right, or Problems, Console and the debugger at the bottom. |
| [`view.zoom`](#viewzoom) | Draws the interface's text and icons larger or smaller, from 0.5 (50 percent) to 3 (300 percent); 1 is the actual size. |
| [`vm.run`](#vmrun) | Builds the open project and calls one QuakeC function in the VM over a mock engine, with globals and the fields of a self edict set first, answering each global and field the call changed and any run error. |

## `checkpoint.create`

Records every file of the open project, as it is on disk, as a checkpoint to restore, in a git store of its own.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `checkpoint.create`.",
  "properties": {
    "label": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "What the checkpoint is for, such as the agent run's task; `checkpoint` when absent.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "CreateCheckpointParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Lists the open project's checkpoints, oldest first.

Parameters:

```json
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
```

## `checkpoint.restore`

Puts every file of the open project back as a checkpoint holds it, removing the files made since and dropping unsaved edits, the open map's among them: the map is read again from its file, or closed when the file was made since.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CheckpointNumber": {
      "description": "A checkpoint's number, from 1, the ref `refs/checkpoints/<n>`; written to JSON as the bare\nnumber.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `checkpoint.restore`.",
  "properties": {
    "number": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/CheckpointNumber",
      "description": "The checkpoint's number."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "number"
  ],
  "title": "RestoreCheckpointParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.apply_fix`

Applies a quick fix `map.issues` gave, as one step with undo.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BrushIndex": {
      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "QuickFix": {
      "description": "A quick fix of an issue.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Delete a brush with no volume, which the compilers drop.",
          "properties": {
            "brush": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
              "description": "The brush."
            },
            "entity": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
              "description": "The entity holding it."
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "remove_brush",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "entity",
            "brush"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Rename a misspelled key to the field it is closest to.",
          "properties": {
            "entity": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
              "description": "The entity."
            },
            "from": {
              "description": "The key as written.",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "rename_key",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "description": "The key to write instead.",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "entity",
            "from",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Set a classname to the class it is closest to.",
          "properties": {
            "classname": {
              "description": "The classname to write.",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "entity": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
              "description": "The entity."
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "set_classname",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "entity",
            "classname"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Place an `info_player_start` at a point inside the map.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "add_player_start",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "origin": {
              "description": "Where.",
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 3,
              "minItems": 3,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "origin"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.apply_fix`.",
  "properties": {
    "fix": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/QuickFix",
      "description": "The fix, as `map.issues` gave it."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "fix"
  ],
  "title": "MapFixParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BrushIndex": {
      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.brush_chamfer`.",

      "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
      "description": "The brush."
    },
    "distance": {
      "description": "How far along each of the edge's faces the bevel starts, in map units.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "description": "The edge's two vertices.",
      "items": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 3,
        "minItems": 3,

      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
```

## `map.brush_clip`

Clips a brush of the open map by the plane through three points, keeping the part behind it, in front of it, or both as two brushes.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BrushIndex": {
      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "Keep": {
      "description": "Which parts of a clipped brush stay.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "back",
          "description": "The part behind the plane, the side its normal points away from.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "front",
          "description": "The part in front of it.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "both",
          "description": "Both, as two brushes.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.brush_clip`.",
  "properties": {
    "brush": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
      "description": "The brush."
    },
    "entity": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
      "description": "The entity holding the brush."
    },
    "keep": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Keep",
      "default": "back",
      "description": "Which parts stay."
    },
    "points": {
      "description": "Three points on the clipping plane; its normal is `(p0 - p1) x (p2 - p1)`, as a\nface's (MAP-3.4).",
      "items": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 3,
        "minItems": 3,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "entity",
    "brush",
    "points"
  ],
  "title": "BrushClipParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.brush_extrude`

Moves a face of a brush along its normal by a distance snapped to the grid, out or in, its texture fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.3).

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BrushIndex": {
      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "ExtrudeMode": {
      "description": "What `map.brush_extrude` does with the face, as TrenchBroom's extrude tool's keys choose\n(P7-08).",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "extrude",
          "description": "The face moves along its normal, the brush's other planes kept.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "split",
          "description": "Out, a new brush of what the extrusion would add; in, the brush cut in two (Ctrl).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "stamp",
          "description": "A new brush, the face and its copy moved out (Ctrl+Alt).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "move",
          "description": "The face's corners move along its normal, the other faces tilting (Alt).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "FaceIndex": {
      "description": "A face's place among its brush's faces, from 0, in file order.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "FaceRef": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A face of the open map: the entity, the brush and the face.",
      "properties": {
        "brush": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
          "description": "The brush."
        },
        "entity": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
          "description": "The entity holding the brush."
        },
        "face": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FaceIndex",
          "description": "The face."
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "entity",
        "brush",
        "face"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "Lock": {
      "description": "Whether a moved brush's textures stay fixed in the world (P6-09, MAP-11.2).",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "locked",
          "description": "Texture lock on: the textures stay where they are in the world.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "free",
          "description": "Texture lock off: the textures move with the brush.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.brush_extrude`.",
  "properties": {
    "by": {
      "description": "How far it moves along its outward normal, snapped to the grid; in when negative.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "face": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/FaceRef",
      "description": "The face."
    },
    "grid": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "The grid `by` snaps to; 16 when not given, 0 for none.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "lock": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Lock",
      "default": "locked",
      "description": "Whether its texture stays fixed in the world; locked when not given."
    },
    "mode": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ExtrudeMode",
      "default": "extrude",
      "description": "What the move does; an extrusion when not given (P7-08)."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "face",
    "by"
  ],
  "title": "BrushExtrudeParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Adds a shape of brushes filling a box, its corners snapped to the grid: a cylinder (solid or hollow), cone, arch, UV or icosahedron spheroid, rock, scalable curve of 12, 24, 48 or 96 sides, or straight or spiral stairs whose default step a player climbs; to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture.

```json
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "Lock": {
      "description": "Whether a moved brush's textures stay fixed in the world (P6-09, MAP-11.2).",

        {
          "const": "locked",
          "description": "Texture lock on: the textures stay where they are in the world.",
          "type": "string"

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

  ],
  "title": "BrushShearParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.brush_subtract`

Subtracts a brush of the open map from every other brush of its entity, then deletes it: the brushes it overlapped become the parts outside it.

Parameters:

```json
{

    "BrushIndex": {
```

```json
{

      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",

    },

      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "Lock": {
      "description": "Whether a moved brush's textures stay fixed in the world (P6-09, MAP-11.2).",

          "const": "locked",
          "description": "Texture lock on: the textures stay where they are in the world.",
          "type": "string"
```

## `map.brushes`

Lists the brushes of an entity of the open map, the world's when none is named: each brush's place, which the map.brush_* tools take, the box around it and its textures; all of them, or those touching a box. The brush tools answer the places of the brushes they make, so this is for brushes whose places are not known: a map someone else built, or after a tool that changed how many brushes the entity has.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",

      "type": "integer"
    }
  },

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.brushes`.",
  "properties": {
    "entity": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null,
      "description": "The entity whose brushes are listed; the world when not given."
    },
    "within": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "Only the brushes whose box touches this one, two opposite corners in either order;\nevery brush when not given.",
      "items": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 3,
        "minItems": 3,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "BrushesParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.build_passage`

```json
          "default": null,

            "string",
            "null"
          ]

          "default": null,

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]

      "default": "none",
```

## `map.check`

Checks a .map: what id's qbsp and ericw-tools read otherwise, and its entities against the project's server QuakeC as the engine reads them: unknown classnames and keys with the closest name, values their field cannot read, and targets and targetnames nothing matches. It reads the file alone, so it says a world that names no WAD is one as id's qbsp does; map.issues and map.find_leaks say whether a texture of the open map is missing.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.check`.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "The `.map` file.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
```

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CompileRegion": {

        {
          "additionalProperties": false,

            "rooms": {
              "items": {

              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "rooms"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The box from `min` to `max`.",
          "properties": {
            "box": {
              "properties": {
                "max": {
                  "description": "Its greatest corner.",
                  "items": {
                    "format": "double",
                    "type": "number"
                  },
                  "maxItems": 3,
                  "minItems": 3,
                  "type": "array"
                },
                "min": {
                  "description": "Its least corner.",
                  "items": {
                    "format": "double",
                    "type": "number"
                  },
                  "maxItems": 3,
                  "minItems": 3,
                  "type": "array"
                }
              },
              "required": [
                "min",
                "max"
              ],
              "type": "object"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "box"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "The parameters of `map.compile`.",
  "properties": {
    "region": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CompileRegion"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null,
```

```json
      "minimum": 0,

      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
```
```json
    "FaceRef": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A face of the open map: the entity, the brush and the face.",
      "properties": {
        "brush": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
          "description": "The brush."
        },
        "entity": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",

        },

        }
      },
```

```json
        "brush",
        "face"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "JustifyTo": {
      "description": "Where `justify` puts the texture.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "left",
          "description": "Its left edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right",
          "description": "Its right edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "top",
          "description": "Its top edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "bottom",
          "description": "Its bottom edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "centre",
          "description": "Its centre on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "UvChoice": {
      "description": "What `map.face_uv` does to each face.",

        {
          "additionalProperties": false,

            },

          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {

          },

            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {

            }
          },

          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {

              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
```

## `map.play_from_here`

Compiles the open map fast, with no vis and fast light, into the project's build, starts the game on it and puts the player's eye at a point, facing a way: the map view's camera (MAP-13), or with no eye the map's own player start. It answers where the player was put, the light there and the entities that stand in the dark; with start paused the game waits there with its monsters not yet awake, for a screenshot of the map as it was built.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CompileRegion": {
      "description": "The part of the open map a compile takes (MAP-16), when it is not the whole map.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The rooms these entities are, or are in, innermost: a layer's or group's own entity is\nthat room, any other entity the room around it (MAP-9.4). The region is the box around\ntheir bounds (MAP-16.1).",
          "properties": {
            "rooms": {
              "items": {
                "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex"
              },
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "rooms"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The box from `min` to `max`.",
          "properties": {
            "box": {
              "properties": {
                "max": {
                  "description": "Its greatest corner.",
                  "items": {
                    "format": "double",
                    "type": "number"
                  },
                  "maxItems": 3,
                  "minItems": 3,
                  "type": "array"
                },
                "min": {
                  "description": "Its least corner.",
                  "items": {
                    "format": "double",
                    "type": "number"
                  },
                  "maxItems": 3,
                  "minItems": 3,
                  "type": "array"
                }
              },
              "required": [
                "min",
                "max"
              ],
              "type": "object"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "box"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "GameStart": {
      "description": "How a game starts once its map has loaded.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "running",
          "description": "The game runs.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "paused",
          "description": "The game is paused before a frame runs (BRIDGE-3.6): every entity is where the map\nput it, the monsters not yet awake, until it is resumed or stepped.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.play_from_here`.",
  "properties": {
    "angles": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "Which way the player faces, pitch, yaw and roll in degrees; when not given, the way\nthe player start faces with no eye, and ahead along x with one.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "eye": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "Where the player's eye goes: the map view's camera. The player's origin is\n`view_ofs` below it, moved up or down to the nearest place its box fits. When not\ngiven the player starts where the map's own first `info_player_start` stands, as\nthe game starts the map; a map with none is refused.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "region": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CompileRegion"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null,
      "description": "Only this part of the map, sealed, so the room being worked on compiles at once\n(MAP-16); the whole map when not given."
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/GameStart",
      "default": "running",
      "description": "Whether the game runs or is left paused where the player was put. Paused, the game\nstarts paused, the player is put in place and one frame is run to show the view from\nthere: `engine.screenshot` then shows the map with every monster where the map put\nit, not yet awake, which is the picture to review a room by; `preview.resume` plays\non. Running when not given."
    }
  },
  "title": "PlayFromHereParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.summary`

A map in short, to review it or compare it with others: the box around its brushes, its brush and entity counts, its entities counted by classname (monsters, lights, items, triggers), its textures counted by face, and its world's keys. The open map, or with a path a .map file read from the disk without opening it; with `most_textures`, only that many textures of the count it gives, which keeps it short when many maps are read. map.list_entities lists each entity; this counts them.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.summary`.",
  "properties": {
    "most_textures": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "Only this many of the textures, the most used first; all of them when not given. A\nfull map names hundreds of textures, so a few is what to ask for when reading many\nmaps. The classnames are never cut: they are the map's monsters, items and triggers.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "A `.map` file to summarise from the disk, which is not opened: the way to read many\nmaps, as when comparing a set of them. The open map when not given.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "SummaryParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Adds frames of another model of the same vertices to the end of a model's own, each by its name: QuakeC's $frame list gains the same names at its end.

Parameters:

```json
{

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `model.add_frames`.",

      "description": "The frames to add, each by its name there, in this order, after the model's own.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "from_path": {
      "description": "The `.mdl` file the frames come from, a model of the same vertices: another copy of\nthe model with other poses.",
      "type": "string"

    "path": {
      "description": "The `.mdl` file to add frames to.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [

    "frames"
  ],
  "title": "AddFramesParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `model.import`

Makes a .mdl model in the project of a mesh in an .obj file (one pose), or an .iqe, .fbx, .md5mesh or .smd file (a frame for each frame of each animation, posed by its skeleton). A mesh with texture coordinates keeps them, on a PNG given as its skin or one colour; one without is laid out front and back, to export, paint and set.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UpAxis": {
      "description": "Which axis of a mesh's file points up.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "y",
          "description": "y is up and -z forward, as most programs write an `.obj`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "z",
          "description": "z is up and x forward, as Quake has them.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `model.import`.",
  "properties": {
    "animation_paths": {
      "default": [],
      "description": "The animations of an `.md5mesh`, its `.md5anim` files, or of an `.smd` model, its\nanimation `.smd` files: a pose for each frame of each, named by the file and the\nframe's number. An `.md5mesh` given none takes the `.md5anim` of its own name beside\nit, when there is one.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "colour": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "The colour of the palette the skin is filled with when no PNG is given; 8 when not\ngiven.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "The `.mdl` file to make of it, in the project; one that is there already is refused.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "png_path": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "A PNG for the skin of a mesh that has texture coordinates, each pixel matched to the\npalette as `model.set_skin` matches one. Its width is a multiple of 4 and its height\nat most 480.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "scale": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "What every position is multiplied by, to make the model the size Quake's are (a\nplayer is 56 units high); 1 when not given.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "skin_size": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "The skin's width and height for a mesh with texture coordinates and no PNG; 128 by\n128 when not given. A mesh without them has a skin of the size its layout needs.",
      "items": {
        "format": "int32",
        "type": "integer"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "source_path": {
      "description": "The mesh to read: an `.obj` file, one pose; an `.iqe` or an `.fbx` file, a pose\nfor each frame of each of its animations; or an `.md5mesh` or an `.smd` model, posed\nby the files of `animation_paths`.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "up": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UpAxis"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null,
      "description": "Which axis of the file is up: y for an `.obj` and an `.fbx`, and z for the others,\nwhen not given. A y-up file is turned so that its -z is forward, Quake's +x, which\nis how programs write a model that faces its viewer's way."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "source_path",
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "ImportParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Recolours a skin of a model by rows of the palette: every pixel of a row becomes the same shade of another row, as the game recolours a player's shirt and trousers.

```json
{

      "description": "Rows of the palette to change, each a row to take and the row to give: the palette is\n16 rows of 16 shades, and a pixel keeps its shade. `[[1, 4]]` turns the browns of row\n1 into the reds of row 4.",
```

```json
{
```

## `project.reference`

The reference to read before writing or debugging QuakeC or building a map, by topic: quakec (the language, how a mod runs, pitfalls), entities (what the engine calls, movetype and solid, the builtins by purpose, what QuakeC does that C does not, debugging), monsters (how a monster is written and every place a new one is added), models (what a model is, and how to recolour, scale and reframe one), maps, workflow (tests and scenarios). Written from id's QuakeC and the engine's specs; a mod's own code comes first where it differs.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Topic": {
      "description": "A topic of the agent reference.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "quakec",
          "description": "The language, how a mod is laid out and run, and its pitfalls.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "entities",
          "description": "What the engine calls, how an entity moves and collides, the builtins by what they\nare for, what the language does that C does not, and debugging.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "monsters",
          "description": "How a monster is written, from id's own, and where a new one must be added.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "models",
          "description": "What a model is, a mod's own models, and how to recolour, scale and reframe one.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "maps",
          "description": "The `.map` format, units, the entities a map needs, textures and leaks.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "workflow",
          "description": "How to work in QuakeC Studio: finding code, changing it, tests and scenarios.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `project.reference`.",
  "properties": {
    "topic": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Topic",
      "description": "The topic to read."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "topic"
  ],
  "title": "ReferenceParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `texture.import`

Imports a PNG image as a texture: quantized to the game's palette with its mip levels, written into the project's own WAD in textures/, in place of a texture of the same name, and that WAD named in the open map's world.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "DitherChoice": {
      "description": "How an imported image is matched to the palette (WAD-7).",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "none",
          "description": "Each pixel to its nearest colour.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "floyd_steinberg",
          "description": "Floyd and Steinberg's error diffusion.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `texture.import`.",
  "properties": {
    "dither": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/DitherChoice",
      "default": "none",
      "description": "How the image is matched to the palette."
    },
    "name": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "The texture's name; the image's file name, without its extension, when not given.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "The PNG image.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "TextureImportParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```
